Subject: Reserved capacity commitment — pricing contingency request

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close on technical fit and want to move to committed capacity, but procurement has raised a concern: GPU spot and supply prices have been volatile and our CFO asked for some protection in the pricing if market GPU costs spike during the term.

Specifically they asked whether Redwood can:
- Add a capped indexation clause (e.g., +/- X% band tied to market GPU index)
- Offer a short-term corridor where discounts are protected if GPU prices rise beyond a threshold

Can you share what contractual options we have for a 12–24 month reserved commitment (we’re leaning to 24 months) and how discounts would be impacted if GPU costs move materially? I can share a template procurement schedule if helpful.

Attached: procurement-requirements-20260929.pdf

Looking forward —
Anne

Anne —

Appreciate the clarity. We can definitely structure a commitment that mitigates CloudSphere’s exposure while keeping unit economics sane for both sides. High-level options (I’ve attached a short overview):

Option A — 12-month fixed-commit (no indexation)
- Firm SKU pricing for the term
- Higher up-front discount than on-demand; limited flexibility for changes
- Best if you prioritize price predictability and shorter contract length

Option B — 24-month tiered commit with GPU-cost collar
- Base discount applied to committed SKUs; quarterly GPU-market index review
- If the GPU index rises > 8% vs baseline, Redwood and customer trigger a price-collar mechanism: either a capped pass-through of delta (up to 4%) or an agreed credit schedule
- Includes right to resize SKUs at 6-month intervals (subject to reallocation fee)

Option C — 24-month hybrid (tiered + overage protection)
- Similar to B but adds a limited credit buffer for a single market shock event in the first 12 months

Next steps I propose: I’ll loop in Marcus (finance/infra) and Laura (sales ops) for a sensitivity run and recommended approval path. If you’re happy, I’ll come back with two clean contract options and a DocuSign-ready summary.

Attachment: commit-options-v1.pdf

—Rishi

Rishi / Laura —

Quick sensitivity notes after modeling CloudSphere’s proposed bands. See attached CSV with scenario outputs. Key takeaways: 

- Baseline (no market movement): 24-mo commit at 22% net discount vs hosted list looks acceptable and preserves margin.
- Moderate GPU uptick (+8% index): If we adopt full pass-through, Redwood margin compresses by ~6ppt. A capped pass-through (max 4%) preserves ~3–4ppt margin, reasonable if we secure a volume-based make-good (credit schedule) tied to usage thresholds.
- Severe shock (+25%): Any pass-through would be painful; better to handle as a pre-negotiated exceptional event with a 30-day re-opener clause and one-time credit on the contract.

Operational asks for contract language:
- Define the GPU index (public vendor index or Redwood internal blended index) and update cadence (quarterly recommended).
- Put hard caps on pass-through percentage and include maximum annualized impact.
- Include an approval gate for rebalancing SKUs at 6 months (sales ops sign-off).

Attachment: fleet-sensitivity-model.csv

If legal signs off on a collar + one-time shock clause, I’m comfortable recommending Option B with capped pass-through (4%) and credit buffer.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Finance, Redwood Inference

Adding Sales Ops perspective —

I recommend we present two firm proposals to CloudSphere:
1) 12-month fixed (Option A) — fast to close, lower discount, no indexation. Approval: AM + Sales Ops.
2) 24-month collar (Option B) — better discount, capped pass-through (4%), one-time buffer credit up to 2% of committed spend for a single qualifying shock. Approval: AM + Finance (Marcus) + VP Sales.

Practical notes:
- Keep SKU change windows at 6 months with a nominal reallocation fee (covers rescheduling and capacity churn).
- Require a 60-day notice period for invoking the collar review so we can pre-plan capacity and avoid sudden fleet reshuffles.
- Prepare a short executive memo for VP Sales and CFO explaining bucketed risk & proposed mitigation.

If Rishi is comfortable, I’ll draft the contract terms to push to legal. We’ll need VP Sales and CFO sign-off for the 24-month collar.

—Laura

Anne / Tariq —

Thanks for the patience while we ran sensitivity and approval checks. Below are the two proposal tracks we can send to legal and procurement today. I’ve attached a concise offer summary (PDF) for your team.

Proposal 1 — 12-month fixed commit (Quick Close)
- Committed SKUs: 50 x A100-equivalent units (reserve pool)
- Term: 12 months
- Discount: 18% off hosted list
- No indexation clause; price locked for term
- Resize: one window at month 6 with reallocation fee

Proposal 2 — 24-month collar commit (Recommended for volume savings)
- Committed SKUs: 50 x A100-equivalent units (reserve pool)
- Term: 24 months
- Discount: 22% off hosted list base
- GPU indexation: quarterly review vs baseline; if index > +8% then capped pass-through up to +4% to the per-token price OR customer elects a credit schedule (customer choice)
- One-time buffer credit: up to 2% of committed spend if a single qualifying shock (>= +20%) occurs in first 12 months
- Resize windows at months 6, 12 (subject to ops lead approval)
- 60-day notice for invoking indexation review

Next steps:
1) Tell me which proposal you prefer and any small redlines.
2) If you want Proposal 2, I’ll route the term sheet to Legal + VP Sales + CFO for sign-off and produce a DocuSign-ready contract.
